transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I keep checking things over and over—boxes, lists, drawers in the condo—before I can move on. I know I’ve already looked, but I still feel like I have to check again. My wife gets frustrated waiting for me to just leave it alone.
Before you check again, do you get an unwanted thought that something bad might happen if you don’t?

Yes. I start thinking maybe I threw away something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool I’ll need in the wrong box. I know it’s probably not likely, but the thought keeps coming back and I can’t quite settle until I check.
Do these thoughts about having thrown away something important feel intrusive and unwanted to you?

Yes, they are. I don’t want to keep thinking about it—I tell myself it’s unlikely—but then I start worrying I threw out something important from my teaching files, or put a tool in the wrong box. It keeps coming back until I check.
On a typical day, how much time do these checking rituals take up?

It’s not all day, but it does take up time—especially when I’m packing things away or trying to leave. I’ll go back through the same boxes, lists, or drawers several times, even though I know I’ve checked them already.
Outside of the checking, do you generally feel a strong need for things to be done in an exact or perfect way?
I’m not sure I’d say I need everything perfect, exactly. It’s more that I want to feel certain I haven’t made a mistake.
Do you wish you could resist the urge to check, but feel unable to stop yourself?

Yes. I tell myself I’ve already checked, and I know I have, but I still go back through the boxes or drawers again. My wife will be waiting for me to leave it alone, and I just feel like I can’t move on until I check one more time.
When you check the boxes or drawers again, does it make the anxiety or uneasy feeling go down, even if only for a moment?
Yes, for a little while. I’ll check the box or drawer again and feel more settled, but then I start wondering if I missed something and end up going back to it.
Do you believe your fear that you may have thrown away something important is exaggerated, or does it seem completely reasonable to you?

I know it’s probably unlikely, but I keep getting this nagging thought that I may have thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or put a needed tool in the wrong box. I tell myself it doesn’t make much sense, but I still can’t quite settle it in my mind.
Have these checking habits significantly interfered with your daily life?

Yes, I think so. Unpacking the condo has taken much longer than it should because I keep needing to verify things. And I’ve been putting off preparing for my library tutoring and even my hobbies, because I feel like I can’t really move on until everything feels checked enough.
Do you also have repetitive unwanted worries about many other parts of life besides the checking, or is it mainly these thoughts about having misplaced or thrown away something important?

It’s mainly the thoughts about the boxes and my old teaching files—whether I threw out something important or put a tool where I won’t be able to find it. I know it’s unlikely, but the thought keeps coming back anyway.
Besides the repeated checking, do you have these unwanted thoughts even at times when you are not checking?

Yes. Even when I’m not going through the boxes, the thought will pop back in—maybe I threw out something important from my teaching files, or put a tool in the wrong box. I know it’s unlikely, but I can’t quite settle it.
